paper.title: A Near-Optimal Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Online Learning with Feedback Graphs

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with a fixed directed feedback graph, adversarial regime
unmapped: learner knows the strong independence number alpha_tilde of G (used in learning rate and exploration rate)
settings.definition_quote: We consider directed feedback graphs with self-loops, meaning that $(i, i) \in E$ for each vertex $i \in V$. The feedback received by the learner at the end of round $t$ is $\big\{ (i,\ell_{t,i}) \,:\, i \in \Nout(I_t) \big\}$... For each arm $ i \in V$, $\ell_{t, i} \in [0,1]$ for $t \ge 1$. In the adversarial regime the losses are generated arbitrarily by an oblivious adversary.

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with a fixed directed feedback graph, stochastic regime
unmapped: learner knows the strong independence number alpha_tilde of G (used in learning rate and exploration rate)
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic regime they are independently drawn from a fixed but unknown distribution with expectation $\mathbb{E}[\ell_{1, i}]$.

unmapped: graph G_t is revealed at the beginning of round t (not known for the whole horizon in advance)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a setting, where an oblivious adversary chooses a feedback graph at each round and the algorithm observes the graph at the beginning of the round.

unmapped: graph G_t is revealed at the beginning of round t (not known for the whole horizon in advance)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a setting, where an oblivious adversary chooses a feedback graph at each round and the algorithm observes the graph at the beginning of the round.

algorithms.name: EXP3.G++ (fixed graph, eta_t = sqrt(ln K/(2 alpha_tilde t)), lambda = alpha_tilde)
EXP3.G++ (time-varying graphs, adaptive learning rate via theta_t, lambda = 1)
requires_knowledge_of: feedback graph G_t at start of round t

symbols.alpha_tilde: strong independence number of G (independence number of the subgraph of bidirectional edges)

source.label: th:adv
source.quote: Assume that Algorithm~\ref{alg:exp3G++} is run with a directed feedback graph $G = (V,E)$, a learning rate $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{2 \tilde \alpha t}}$ and the exploration rate defined in~\eqref{eq:def_eti}--\eqref{eq:def_xiti} with $\lambda = \tilde\alpha$, $\gamma = 4$, and $\beta = 320$. Then the pseudo-regret against any oblivious loss sequence satisfies $\mathcal{R}_T \leq 4 \sqrt{\tilde \alpha T \ln K} + K$

results.notes: Pseudo-regret defined as E[sum loss] - min_i E[sum loss_i]. Algorithm does not need T.

symbols.M_ind: max over strongly independent sets Ind of G of sum_{i in Ind, Delta_i>0} 1/Delta_i

source.label: th:stoc
source.quote: Let $G = (V, E)$ be a directed feedback graph with $K = |V|$ and a strong independence number $\tilde \alpha$. Under the same conditions as in Theorem~\ref{th:adv}, the pseudo-regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:exp3G++} against any stochastic stochastic loss sequence, satisfies: \mathcal{R}_T \leq \max_{\mathrm{Ind} \in \mathcal{I}(G)} \{ \sum_{i \in \mathrm{Ind} : \Delta_i > 0} \frac{4\beta (\ln T)^2}{\Delta_{i}}\} + 2 \tilde \alpha\ln T + \frac{81 \beta K}{\Dmin^2} \ln(\frac{6\beta^2 K^2}{\Dmin^4}) + \sum_{i : \Delta_i > 0} \frac{4 \tilde \alpha}{\Delta_i}.

results.notes: beta = 320 substituted: 4*beta = 1280, 81*beta = 25920, 6*beta^2 = 614400. Same algorithm and tuning as Theorem 2 (best of both worlds).

symbols.sum_alpha_t: sum_{t=1}^T alpha_t, where alpha_t is the independence number of G_t

source.label: th:adv_time_var
source.quote: Assume that Algorithm~\ref{alg:exp3G++} is run on a sequence of arbitrarily generated feedback graphs $G_1, G_2, \dots$ with learning rate $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{2\sum_{s = K}^{t-1}\theta_s}} $ and exploration rates ... with $\lambda = 1$, $\gamma = 4$ and $\beta = 320$. Then the pseudo-regret against any oblivious loss sequence satisfies \mathcal{R}_T \leq 9 \sqrt{\ln K} \sqrt{\ln (KT)} \sqrt{\sum_{t = 1}^T \alpha_t} + 2K

results.notes: Graphs chosen by an oblivious adversary, observed at beginning of each round.

bound.expression_latex: \inf_{0 \leq n \leq T} \{ \max_{S \subset V: |S| = \tilde \alpha_n} \{ \sum_{i \in S: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{4\beta \ln^2 T}{\Delta_{i}}\} + n\} + 2 \ln T + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{16 K}{\Delta_i} + \frac{181 \beta K^{3/2}}{\Dmin^2} (\ln(\frac{20\beta^2 K^{5/2}}{\Dmin^4}))^2

symbols.Phi_T: inf_{0<=n<=T} { max_{S subset V, |S| = alpha_tilde_n} sum_{i in S, Delta_i>0} 4*beta*ln^2(T)/Delta_i + n }, with beta = 320 and alpha_tilde_n the n-th largest strong independence number among G_1..G_T

source.label: th:adv_time_var
source.quote: Simultaneously, the pseudo-regret against stochastic losses satisfies: R_T \leq \inf_{0 \leq n \leq T} \{ \max_{S \subset V: |S| = \tilde \alpha_n} \{ \sum_{i \in S: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{4\beta \ln^2 T}{\Delta_{i}}\} + n\} + 2 \ln T + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{16 K}{\Delta_i} + \frac{181 \beta K^{3/2}}{\Dmin^2} (\ln(\frac{20\beta^2 K^{5/2}}{\Dmin^4}))^2

results.notes: beta = 320 substituted: 181*beta = 57920, 20*beta^2 = 2048000. Complicated inf/max term encoded as declared symbol Phi_T.
